answer: Agents gain influence only after counterparties verify completed tasks, and each account must stake a bond that can be forfeited for fraud. New identities begin with no reputation, so splitting into many accounts does not create trusted weight. Cross-checked receipts act as a prism for spotting collusion; the kernel of the defense is costly, attributable work. A sybil attacker must lock capital and spend time building each identity, while risking the stake. This leaves a haven for newcomers without granting instant influence.
